reason: All key premises are directly and accurately supported by the cited evidence (E1–E3), which describe the same two-step Joule-heating protocol, the disorder-to-order transition, the prevention of growth/agglomeration, and the thermodynamic driving force.
premises: Rapid Joule heating to ~1100 K for tens of ms produces disordered solid-solution HEA nanoparticles from multiple metal salts
A subsequent dwell at ~1100 K for ~5 min enables a disorder-to-order transition to an intermetallic (e.g., L10) phase
The ~5 min dwell is short enough to avoid nanoparticle growth/agglomeration
Rapid cooling (~10^4 K/s) after the dwell preserves the ordered structure and small particle size
The disorder-to-order transition is thermodynamically driven and overcomes kinetic constraints
